points.heading: Practice -ir
points.body:
Close the week’s deepen path with **-ir**: **vivir → vivo, vives, vive**. Add **escribir** and **abrir** (abro, abres, abre).

Build a city chart: yo **vivo** aquí, tú **vives** cerca, él **vive** lejos. Then rewrite the same chart with **escribir**.

Review all three families in one glance: cantar / comer / vivir for yo only, then for tú only. Your ear should catch -o, then -as/-es, then -a/-e.

Compare two short examples out loud. Say what changes and what stays the same.

Write one sentence in your own words before you start the practice task.

Say the key idea without looking, then check whether any important detail is missing.

Teach this point to someone at home with a new example you invent.

Compare two short examples out loud. Say what changes and what stays the same.

Practice: Your turn. Fill a 3×3 grid: rows cantar, comer, vivir; columns yo, tú, él.

Common mistake: Writing «yo vivés» or mixing -ir with -ar endings. Keep -ir present as -o/-es/-e for these persons.

lesson.summary: In this lesson, you will use Spanish verb endings to say who does an action.
lesson.memoryPhrase: Spanish families: **-ar** (cantar → canto, cantas, canta), **-er** (comer → como, comes, come), **-ir** (vivir → vivo, vives, vive).
lesson.weekRecap: Spanish families: -ar (cantar), -er (comer), -ir (vivir). Conjugate for yo, tú, and él in the present.
lesson.priorDayRecap: Yesterday you practiced -er forms with comer, beber, and leer.
